title: docs(pm-skill): release-aftercare duties — the PM window past MERGED (#11134)
body:
Fixes #11134

The pm-dispatch landing window ends at MERGED — which is not the moment a user gets
anything. Nothing in the skill covered what a lane PM still owes after a tagged release
rolls to production. Two days of cloud release operations (2026-08-21/23) hit the same
post-release traps repeatedly, each living only in one operator's memory.

## What lands

A new references page, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/release-aftercare.md`
(58 lines), one line per duty where the duty fits on one:

- **A. Every fleet roll re-draws container placement.** Read placement first, then
  latency, against the lane's perf gate — a region constraint bounds the draw but does
  not pick the city (measured, same ENAM: Ashburn ~4ms / Atlanta ~17ms / Houston ~35ms
  per leg, a 9x spread), and at the measured `server ≈ 33 + 23 × RTT` shape a 35ms leg
  is ~870ms per request against a ≤200ms gate. Two counter-intuitive physics, with the
  protocol whose order cannot be swapped: **placement follows the WAKER**, not
  `locationHint` (re-rolls woken from a California operator machine drew Houston
  repeatedly; waking via a us-east CI runner drew Ashburn first try), and **measuring
  contaminates the next draw** (a probe issued mid-swap becomes the new instance's
  waker) — so: rollout → zero operator HTTP → wake via the us-east runner → read the CF
  instances API for the city → only then measure.
- **B. One real user-path probe after any prod roll.** Not `/health` 200, not a green
  deploy job, not a synthetic E2E: the platform SSO hop failed for every real user for
  five weeks (last successful token exchange 2026-07-17, found 2026-08-22) while health
  checks and the E2E both stayed green — the E2E logged in with email+password and never
  ran the exchange.
- **C. Hand-fixes to live state are a tourniquet.** Before applying one, name WHO
  replays that state and WHEN (seed / reseed / migration / boot binder) and write both
  on the card; the replay-layer fix is the real card, and the fixed code must ship
  before the next replay event or the incident re-opens.
- **D. Orphaned-loop resumption.** A long-running background loop's last recorded intent
  is not the current live state — the first action on resume is always to re-read live
  state, never to continue from that intent.
- **E. Honesty clause.** When a later measurement falsifies a factual assertion in a
  merged PR body, the correction is posted to the card publicly — not merely known.
  Merged is not verified.

Plus **one pointer** from `references/landing-operations.md`, after its MERGED-tracking
material.

## Declared file surface

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/release-aftercare.md` | new page, 58 lines |
| `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md` | the one pointer, **zero line delta** |
| `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` | one CEILINGS row + its provenance comment |

`SKILL.md` is deliberately untouched. The third file is in the surface *because* of the
ratchet accounting below, and is declared here for that reason.

## Ratchet accounting — paid per remedy, no raise

`CEILINGS` enumerates references pages individually, so a new page needs its own row.
Two separate bills, both paid without a maintainer ruling:

1. **The new page** gets its row at its landed line count — `release-aftercare.md`, 58,
   headroom 0, the same convention as every entry around it.
2. **`landing-operations.md` was at its ceiling with headroom 0**, so a physically new
   pointer line would have crossed it. Instead the pointer **rides existing slack** on
   that file's last MERGED-tracking line (36 → 104 bytes, inside the file's own wrap
   width): the file stays at **82 lines**, its ceiling is untouched. No re-wrap, no cut
   of surviving content, no raised roof — the lane charter bans the first two as payment
   and the ratchet header requires a maintainer ruling for the third.

The ratchet's own verdict lines at the pushed commit:


carries `skip-changeset` per convention.
